thread.title: Apple ( AAPL ) has a cash problem. The $250B that is parked

author: Eric Oetjen
title: Apple ( AAPL ) has a cash problem. The $250B that is parked
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) has a cash problem. The $250B that is parked overseas will be boarding a one-way trip back to the US this year. This cash has been doing nothing for APPL, with $210B invested in low returning treasuries and corporate bonds and the rest depreciating as cash.
The situation becomes even more dire for investors when considering opportunity cost of sitting on its cash when APPL has sported a historical return on investment and equity of 18.5% and 37.5% , respectively. As a shareholder, seeing these numbers while their cash sits idle makes me cringe.
Fortunately, AAPL seems to share this concern and has promised to put its net cash position (cash less liabilities) of $163B to good use per the latest earnings call :
"Our current net cash position is $163 billion. And given the increased financial and operational flexibility from the access to our foreign cash, we are targeting to become approximately net cash neutral over time."
However, this presents a separate issue of how best to use this cash to unlock shareholder value. What are some likely options? Again, AAPL is one step ahead of us, hinting at buybacks, dividend, or acquisitions. Depending on whether you're a dividend investor or growth investor, AAPL's next moves will offer excitement or heartbreak. We'll look at the probability of each move as it relates to long-term shareholders and how each move will affect APPL's share price. 
Acquisitions This is the least likely option that will move AAPL's stock price, although it offers the most long term growth potential. For one, it avoids the costs and confusion associated with high profile mergers, and two reduces the cost risk of the merger flopping. For dividend investors who simply want to milk the AAPL cash cow, acquisitions represent potential deferred dividends.
